name: Asklepiadai
note: The physicians: Asklepios and the line that carried medicine to Troy

Asklepios.note: Cut from his dead mother's body and taught medicine by the centaur Cheiron. He grew so good at it that he raised the dead, and Zeus killed him with a thunderbolt for it. Roman: AESCULAPIUS. The rod with the single snake is still the emblem of medicine everywhere -- and is not the caduceus, which is Hermes' and has two. Apollod. 3.10.3-4

Hygieia.note: Daughter of Asklepios: health itself, and the word HYGIENE. Paus. 1.23.4

Panakeia.note: Her sister: the all-healing, and the word PANACEA. Aristophanes Plutus 701

Machaon.note: Son of Asklepios and the army's surgeon at Troy, who cut the arrow out of Menelaos. Il. 4.192-219

Podaleirios.note: His brother, the other physician of the Greek camp. Il. 2.729-733

unions.note: Asklepios is a god and his sons are men in the Greek camp at Troy: the gap is the distance between a healing cult and the war it is dated by.
Unfaithful while carrying his child; the white crow that told him was scorched black for it, and is black still. Apollod. 3.10.3
